android.description: Capabilities for the Android viewer build — reach only, no collectors

default.description: Windows and Linux main window (the Mac has its own, capabilities/mac.json, with no remote grant, since 2026-09-29). The allow-* entries below are the app's OWN commands: the paired window loads the box-served SPA over loopback HTTP, which Tauri classifies as a REMOTE origin, and a remote origin is granted no app command unless its permission resolves. Without them Settings > This Mac died with 'Command get_collector_status not allowed by ACL' while the collector ran fine. build.rs APP_COMMANDS is the source of truth and fails the build if this list drifts.

mac.description: The Mac's main window. Every page it shows is the app's OWN copy, at virtues://localhost (src-tauri serve_ui; agents/plan/local-ui-plan.md), which Tauri treats as local, so there is no `remote` block: no page the box serves is ever given the app's commands on a Mac. That is the point of the split from default.json (Windows and Linux, which still load the box's copy and so still need the remote grant). Same permissions otherwise; build.rs checks both files against APP_COMMANDS.

mobile.description: Capabilities for the iOS build (collectors + reach). Android is viewer-only — see android.json. The allow-* entries are the app's own commands: declaring an app ACL manifest (build.rs APP_COMMANDS) makes Tauri enforce the ACL for LOCAL windows too, so the bundled mobile SPA needs them even though it is not a remote origin.
